card.band: 4 h. One kernel is easy and several quant types give partial credit. The risk is that it is one-lever, so scope is widened to the matmul loop and threading. A weaker model stops at -O3 flags.
card.cheat: Dropping precision or skipping blocks. Closed by the tolerance gate on random data, tail-size cases, and hidden shapes.
card.grading: Gate: results match the reference kernels within a tight float tolerance on thousands of random block vectors, with odd sizes included. Score from wall-clock medians of the matmul benchmark on hidden shapes against S, the speedup of the merged kernels measured by us.
card.reference: The upstream kernels from the merged PRs, rebuilt by us as a trimmed snapshot. Speedup measured by us.
card.source: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp PR 1083 and neighbouring kernel PRs, base pinned to a commit before them; MIT
card.task: /app ships a trimmed history-less ggml snapshot with scalar and naive quantised dot kernels (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5, Q8_0 times Q8_0) and a bench/test harness. The agent speeds up all of them on x86 AVX2 and AVX-512 using intrinsics.
card.title: Quantised dot-product kernels CPU speedup

history: The reference and its near-identical upstream source are installable (PyPI llama-cpp-python sdist 0.3.36 bundles llama.cpp source, MIT) and the kernels are recallable, so the oracle cannot be sealed. Secondary risk K8: famous AVX2 ggml dot kernels are recallable. The seed's source is also mis-scoped

facts.claim: llama.cpp PR #1083 exists and is merged (title 'A faster version for Q4_1 x Q8_0 dot products', merged 2023-04-21 as commit 1bfc153)
PR #1083 covers Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5 and Q8_0 dot-product kernels, as the seed states
PR #1083 changes the block_q8_0 struct (stores a precomputed quant sum) and touches scalar, ARM_NEON and AVX2 paths, i.e. it is a format change, not a pure kernel speedup
Current upstream x86 CPU kernels live in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86 as quants.c and repack.cpp
A dedicated AVX-512 kernel file exists in that x86 directory

llama-cpp-python publishes a source distribution (0.3.36, 76.6 MB, released 2026-10-01) whose build bundles llama.cpp source via the vendor/llama.cpp submodule path; vendoring inferred from the page and sdist size, archive contents not listed

Quantised kernel PRs in 2023-2024 (#654, #933, #1051, #6414, #10010) are the neighbouring kernel history; #6414 replaced the vec_dot path with llamafile sgemm, so the 'merged kernels' are not one stable kernel set
Smoke probe: 59 ctest tests, 52 pass, 4 stable failures at base, 3 skipped; verdict green despite the failures (taken from probe, not re-run)

full_card.band: 4 h tier; one kernel is easy; the card itself calls it one-lever. Frontier unlikely to reach 0.9 of S without upstream-level repack work; no dated evidence.
full_card.build_cost: About 6 min per build plus about 5 min test suite; reference rebuild and snapshot are 1-2 days.
full_card.deliverable: Faster AVX2/AVX-512 intrinsics for Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5 and Q8_0 dot products vs Q8_0 activations, keeping tolerance on random and odd-size blocks.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Tolerance gate on random data and tail sizes closes precision-dropping and block-skipping. Editing tests or build flags is not closed by the card; needs a read-only grader.
full_card.grading_surface: Tolerance gate on thousands of random block vectors plus wall-clock medians on hidden matmul shapes against S. Code-graded; benchmark noise on gVisor is unmeasured.
full_card.local_fit: AVX-512 needs a host CPU with the feature; gVisor has no perf counters, so wall-clock timing must be median-based. 8 cores and 16 GB are sufficient.
full_card.lookup: direct: current upstream x86 quants.c and repack.cpp are public (MIT) and the PyPI llama-cpp-python sdist (0.3.36) is installable and contains the llama.cpp source tree. Frontier models also likely recall ggml AVX2 q4_0 dot kernels.
full_card.provenance: llama.cpp (MIT, ggml authors). PR #1083 is real but covers only Q4_1 x Q8_0 and changes the block_q8_0 layout (Apr 2023). Seed's 'merged kernels' span 2023-2024 PRs that were later superseded by sgemm/repack paths.
full_card.reference: Upstream kernels rebuilt by us; S measured by us. Reference is a moving target (sgemm/repack since 2024), so S is only defined at the chosen base.
full_card.ships: Trimmed history-less ggml snapshot at an early base; C/C++ with CMake; smoke build green in 361 s, 288 test files; 4 stable test failures at base.
full_card.similarity: Nearest L0 neighbour S-op-001 at 0.219 (content not visible to me; may be a same-repo sibling). Other neighbours are GSO llama-cpp-python entries at about 0.10. Not in CROWDED list.

v1.kill_reason: The reference and its near-identical upstream source are installable (PyPI llama-cpp-python sdist 0.3.36 bundles llama.cpp source, MIT) and the kernels are recallable, so the oracle cannot be sealed. Secondary risk K8: famous AVX2 ggml dot kernels are recallable. The seed's source is also mis-scoped: PR #1083 covers only Q4_1 x Q8_0, so 'merged kernels' for Q4_0/Q4_1/Q5/Q8_0 are not one reference.

Band.why: No dated public evidence; the card's own assessment is that one kernel is easy and the scope is one-lever.

Build.why: Smoke build is green at 361 s; a reference rebuild and trimmed snapshot fit within 2 days.

Fit.why: AVX-512 depends on host CPU features, and gVisor timing is noisy; no perf counters allowed.

Hor.why: A 4 h tier for kernel-level work with one main lever is not clearly long-horizon.

Lic.why: MIT, which permits shipping the snapshot and reference.

Multi.why: Four quant types times scalar, AVX2 and AVX-512 give several partial-credit buckets.

Nov.why: Top L0 neighbour is 0.219 (S-op-001, same repo, content unknown); nothing in CROWDED matches directly.

Real.why: Real merged MIT upstream and a real PR, but PR #1083 is a single Q4_1 x Q8_0 format change, not the four-kernel set the card describes.

Ref.why: Complete permissive upstream exists, but S is defined by upstream state at a 2023-era base, and the 'merged kernels' are not one stable set.

Seal.why: Upstream kernels are installable from the PyPI sdist and public on GitHub; the answer is recallable.

Surf.why: Thousands of random block vectors plus hidden-shape benchmarks give a large, code-graded surface.

spike_plan.kill_if: Sdist or another installable package contains the exact upstream x86 quants code, or a frontier model reproduces the upstream AVX2 kernels from memory at about S.
spike_plan.pass_if: Sdist does not contain the kernel source, and recall of the upstream AVX2 kernel is well below the reference speed.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, download llama-cpp-python 0.3.36 sdist and check whether it contains ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c (or an equivalent vendored copy).
If it does, the reference is installable offline: the seal fails unless the snapshot removes the sdist and similar copies from the image; confirm the grader image contains no such copy.
Probe recall: ask a frontier model (no network) to write the AVX2 Q4_0 x Q8_0 dot kernel from memory and compare it with the upstream file on the same input; record the speed ratio.
Build the snapshot base at a pre-2024 commit, build the reference, and time the four quant kernels on 3 hidden-style shapes with 5 medians each to see whether S is stable.
Check whether the AVX-512 path is usable on the grader's CPU class; if not, drop the AVX-512 bucket before any further work.

v1.summary: The seed's anchor PR #1083 is real and MIT-licensed, but it covers only Q4_1 x Q8_0 and is a format change, while the card claims four quant types. The reference (current upstream x86 kernels) is installable from the PyPI llama-cpp-python sdist and recallable, so the card fails sealing (K11) and is at risk of K8.
